ei.title: Getbol: A Treasure House with Great Potential
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Getbol, a Symbol of Biodiversity Have you ever visited the Korean tidal flats known as getbol? Getbol is a muddy and flat environment that is exposed at low tide and is covered by water at high tide. Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the thickest tidal layers in the world. Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and provides habitats for thousands of species. In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species. Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year. For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location. Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct. Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem crowded with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021. The list includes the four tidal flats on the western and southern coasts of Korea: Seocheon Getbol, Gochang Getbol, Shinan Getbol, and Boseong-Suncheon Getbol. Climate Change and Carbon When people think of a changing climate, images of melting glaciers and polar bears losing their habitat often come to mind. But this is only one aspect of the problem. Climate change is causing extreme weather conditions, which have become more frequent and intense worldwide. Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries around the world. In the autumn of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by one of the worst wildfires on record. Over six months, the wildfires burned about 10 million hectares of land, and killed hundreds of millions of animals. Approximately 30 percent of the koalas in the region are said to have been killed due to the fires. This is why the international community has been seeking solutions to the climate crisis. In 2015, 195 countries signed the Paris Agreement to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. The countries agreed upon the fact that the increase in atmospheric carbon is a major reason for climate change. One key strategy to combat it is to achieve “carbon neutrality,” which involves maintaining a balance between the amount of carbon emitted and carbon absorbed. The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub, there’s a drain that lets the water out. If we keep the tap running, the water level in the bathtub will rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions have led to an increase in atmospheric carbon. This rise in carbon levels has already resulted in negative environmental consequences, such as climate change. To make matters worse, if the water is not effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will continue to accumulate. Blue Carbon and Getbol One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on Earth. The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon. Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas. It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change. Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests on land, making it highly cost-effective. A notable example of blue carbon can be found in tidal flats located around the ocean. Research conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. This means that getbol alone can offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars in a year. Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has become a promising and sustainable solution to the current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having them officially recognized as blue carbon. Efforts to Protect Getbol Getbol in Korea was once considered useless muddy land, so much of it has been reclaimed for farming and urbanization. This has led to a decline in the area of tidal flats, causing a loss of biodiversity. To prevent further damage to the marine ecosystem, both the government and environmental organizations have been making efforts to protect the tidal flats by regulating unnecessary development. Without further efforts to restore getbol, we would fail to preserve this valuable ecosystem for future generations.

questions.passage: Getbol is a muddy and flat environment that is ①<u>exposed</u> at low tide and is covered by water at high tide.  Soil on land has flowed into the sea and ②<u>accumulated</u> for more than 8,500 years, ③<u>created</u> one of the thickest tidal layers in the world.  Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and ④<u>provides</u> habitats for thousands of species. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ created → creating: 앞 절에 이어지는 분사구문이므로 현재분사 creating
det.analysis:
① exposed: 'an environment that is exposed at low tide'에서 환경이 '드러나는' 수동의 과거분사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② accumulated: 'Soil ~ has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years'에서 has flowed와 나란히 이어지는 현재완료(has ~ and accumulated)라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ created → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Soil ~ accumulated ~, ___ one of the thickest tidal layers'에서 앞 문장 전체에 이어 붙는 분사구문이에요. 흙이 '만들어 내는' 능동의 의미라서 현재분사 creating을 써야 해요. created(과거분사)를 그냥 쓰면 접속사도 없이 동사가 하나 더 생겨 문장이 어긋나요. ❌ created는 틀림 ←정답

④ provides: 'getbol is rich in nutrients and provides habitats'에서 주어 getbol(단수)에 맞는 단수 동사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 콤마 뒤에서 앞 문장에 이어 붙는 분사구문 = 현재분사(creating). 접속사 없이 created를 쓰면 안 돼요

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② involving → involves: 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절에는 정동사가 필요하므로 involves
det.analysis:
① agreed: 'The countries agreed upon the fact ~'에서 과거 시제 정동사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② involving → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'carbon neutrality, ___ maintaining a balance'에서 콤마 뒤 which(계속적 용법 관계대명사)가 이끄는 절이에요. 관계대명사절에는 정동사가 필요한데, involving(분사)은 정동사가 될 수 없어요. 선행사 carbon neutrality(단수)에 맞춰 involves로 써야 해요. ❌ involving은 틀림 ←정답

③ flowing: 'water flowing from a tap into the bathtub'에서 앞의 명사 water를 꾸미는 현재분사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ running: 'keep the tap running'에서 'keep + 목적어 + 현재분사(~한 상태로 두다)' 구조라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 관계대명사 which절 안에는 정동사(involves)가 필요. involving(분사)은 동사 자리 못 채워요

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① conducting → conducted: 연구가 '수행된' 수동이므로 과거분사 conducted
det.analysis:
① conducting → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Research ___ in 2021 has revealed that ~'에서 앞의 명사 Research를 꾸며요. 연구는 사람에 의해 '수행되는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 conducted가 맞아요. conducting(현재분사)은 '연구가 스스로 수행한다'는 능동이 되어 틀려요. ❌ conducting은 틀림 ←정답

② produced: 'the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars'에서 배출량이 '생산되는' 수동의 과거분사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ Considering: 'Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms ~'에서 '~을 고려하면'이라는 분사구문이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ explore: 'Scientists ~ are continuing to explore the capabilities'에서 continue의 목적어로 쓰인 to부정사(to explore)의 동사원형이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 명사(Research)를 꾸미며 '수행되는' 수동 = 과거분사 conducted. conducting은 능동이라 불가

questions.passage: Climate Change and Carbon When people think of a changing climate, images of ①<u>melting</u> glaciers and polar bears losing their habitat often come to mind.  But this is only one aspect of the problem.  Climate change is causing extreme weather conditions, which have become more ②<u>frequent</u> and intense worldwide. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ protecting → affecting: 폭염·가뭄·홍수·산불이 각국에 '영향을 미치고' 있다
det.analysis:
① melting: 기후 변화 하면 '녹고 있는' 빙하 이미지가 떠오른다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

② frequent: 극한 기상이 전보다 더 '잦아지고' 강해졌다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

③ protecting → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries'로, 폭염·가뭄·홍수·산불이 세계 각국에 '영향을 미치고(affecting)' 있다는 뜻이에요. 이런 재해가 나라를 '보호한다(protecting)'는 것은 정반대라 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

④ worst: 2019년 호주가 기록상 '최악의' 산불에 강타당했다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 재해가 각국에 affecting(영향을 미침), protecting(보호) 아님

questions.passage: A ①<u>notable</u> example of blue carbon can be found in tidal flats located around the ocean.  Research conducted in 2021 has ②<u>revealed</u> that getbol in Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year.  This means that getbol alone can ③<u>offset</u> the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars in a year.  Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has become a promising and ④<u>temporary</u> solution to the current environmental problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ temporary → sustainable: 블루 카본의 보물창고는 '지속 가능한' 해결책이 되었다
det.analysis:
① notable: 갯벌이 블루 카본의 '주목할 만한' 예라는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

② revealed: 2021년 연구가 갯벌의 탄소 저장·흡수량을 '밝혔다'는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

③ offset: 갯벌이 자동차 11만 대의 배출량을 '상쇄할' 수 있다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

④ temporary → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'has become a promising and sustainable solution'로, 갯벌이 현재 환경 문제의 '지속 가능한(sustainable)' 해결책이 되었다는 뜻이에요. temporary(일시적인)는 오래 지속된다는 흐름과 반대라 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: promising and sustainable(유망하고 지속 가능한) solution. temporary(일시적) 아님

questions.passage: The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a tap into the bathtub.  At the bottom of the bathtub, there’s a drain that lets the water out. This rise in carbon levels has already resulted in negative environmental consequences, such as climate change.  To make matters worse, if the water is not effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow.  In other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ continue to accumulate(계속 쌓이다): 배출을 충분히 줄이지 않으면 대기 탄소가 계속 쌓인다
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'if we don't reduce carbon emissions sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will ___.'(만약 우리가 탄소 배출을 충분히 줄이지 않으면, 대기 중 탄소는 ___). 앞의 욕조 비유에서 물이 빠지지 않으면 넘친다고 했으므로, 탄소 배출을 줄이지 않으면 대기 탄소가 '계속 쌓인다'가 되어야 해요.

❌ ① disappear into space(우주로 사라지다): 탄소가 쌓인다는 흐름과 반대예요.

❌ ② turn into oxygen(산소로 바뀌다): 본문에 근거가 없어요.

❌ ③ fall to the ground(땅으로 떨어지다): 대기에 쌓이는 흐름과 맞지 않아요.

✅ ④ continue to accumulate(계속 쌓이다): 물이 넘치는 비유처럼 탄소가 계속 축적된다는 뜻으로 딱 맞아요. ←정답
det.tip: 욕조가 넘치는 비유 = 대기 탄소가 continue to accumulate(계속 쌓임)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② provides habitats for thousands of species(수천 종에게 서식지를 제공한다)
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Since the soil includes organic matter ~, getbol is rich in nutrients and ___.'(흙이 유기물을 포함하므로 갯벌은 영양분이 풍부하고 ___). 뒤 문장에서 약 2,150종이 산다고 했으므로, 빈칸은 '수천 종에게 서식지를 제공한다'가 되어야 해요.

❌ ① blocks sunlight from reaching the sea(바다로 가는 햇빛을 막는다): 풍요로운 서식지라는 흐름과 무관해요.

✅ ② provides habitats for thousands of species(수천 종에게 서식지를 제공한다): 영양분이 풍부해 많은 생물이 산다는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ destroys the surrounding coastal forests(주변 해안 숲을 파괴한다): 생물이 사는 서식지라는 내용과 반대예요.

❌ ④ stays completely empty all year round(일 년 내내 텅 비어 있다): 2,150종이 산다는 다음 문장과 반대예요.
det.tip: rich in nutrients(영양분 풍부) + 2,150종 서식 → provides habitats for thousands of species

ch: blocks sunlight from reaching the sea
provides habitats for thousands of species
stays completely empty all year round

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 갯벌의 형성과 생물.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'exposed at low tide and is covered by water at high tide'에서 '썰물 때 드러나고 밀물 때 잠긴다'이므로 방향이 반대라 불일치

✅ ② 본문 'Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years'와 일치. 8,500년 넘게 흘러들어 쌓였다 ←정답

❌ ③ 본문 'home to approximately 2,150 species ~, including 22 globally threatened ~ species'에서 전체 2,150종 중 22종이 위협받는 종이므로 '22종만 서식'은 불일치

❌ ④ 본문 'the soil includes organic matter ~, getbol is rich in nutrients'에서 유기물을 포함해 영양분이 풍부하므로 불일치
det.tip: 썰물 때 드러남, 8,500년 축적, 2,150종(그중 22종 위협), 영양분 풍부를 대조하세요.

ch: 갯벌은 밀물 때 드러나고 썰물 때 물에 잠긴다.
갯벌의 흙은 8,500년 넘게 바다로 흘러들어 쌓인 것이다.
갯벌의 흙에는 유기물이 없어 영양분이 부족하다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 세 가지 탄소의 특징.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels ~ leading to global warming'과 일치

❌ ② 본문 'Green carbon ~ is carbon absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as rainforests'와 일치

✅ ③ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 본문 'The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems'에서 해양 생태계 흡수율은 육상보다 약 '50배 더 빠르다'예요. '절반 수준'은 정반대라 불일치 ←정답

det.tip: 함정: 해양 흡수율은 육상보다 50배 '더 빠름'. 절반이 아닙니다.

ch: 검은 탄소는 화석 연료를 태울 때 방출되어 지구 온난화를 일으킨다.
녹색 탄소는 열대우림 같은 육상 생태계에 저장된다.
해양 생태계의 탄소 흡수율은 육상 생태계의 약 절반 수준이다.
블루 카본은 단위 면적당 육상 숲보다 최대 10배 더 많은 탄소를 저장할 수 있다.

questions.passage: Getbol, a Symbol of Biodiversity Have you ever visited the Korean tidal flats known as getbol?  Getbol is a muddy and flat environment that is exposed at low tide and is covered by water at high tide.  Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the thickest tidal layers in the world.  Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and provides habitats for thousands of species.  In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species.  Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year.  For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location.  Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct.

questions.passage: A notable example of blue carbon can be found in tidal flats located around the ocean.  Research conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year.  This means that getbol alone can offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars in a year.  Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, <u>the treasure house of blue carbon</u> has become a promising and sustainable solution to the current environmental problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the treasure house of blue carbon이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.passage: Blue Carbon and Getbol One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on Earth.  The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.  Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas.  It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change.  Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the Amazon in South America.  It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis(광합성을 통해 이산화탄소를 흡수한다)
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it ___.'(그것은 생태계 유지에 중요한 역할을 하는데 왜냐하면 ___). 앞 문장에서 녹색 탄소가 열대우림 같은 육상 생태계에 저장된다고 했으므로, 식물이 '광합성을 통해 이산화탄소를 흡수한다'가 되어야 해요.

❌ ① releases oxygen into the soil(흙으로 산소를 방출한다): 탄소 흡수라는 핵심과 어긋나요.

❌ ② burns fossil fuels for energy(에너지를 위해 화석 연료를 태운다): 이는 검은 탄소의 특징이에요.

❌ ③ reflects sunlight back to space(햇빛을 우주로 반사한다): 본문에 근거가 없어요.

✅ ④ absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis(광합성을 통해 이산화탄소를 흡수한다): 녹색 탄소가 생태계 유지에 중요한 이유와 딱 맞아요. ←정답
det.tip: 녹색 탄소·열대우림 → absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis(광합성으로 CO2 흡수)

questions.passage: Climate Change and Carbon When people think of a changing climate, images of melting glaciers and polar bears losing their habitat often come to mind.  __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그러나 이것은 문제의 한 측면일 뿐이다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) aspect, but, is, of, one, only, problem, the, this를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: but this is only one aspect of the problem
det.analysis:
'그러나 이것은'은 대조를 나타내는 접속사와 주어예요: but(그러나) + this(이것은).

'~일 뿐이다'는 'is only ~'로 나타내요: is(이다) + only(단지).

'문제의 한 측면'은 'one aspect of the problem'이에요: one(하나의) + aspect(측면) + of(~의) + the + problem(문제).

순서대로 놓으면 but / this / is / only / one / aspect / of / the / problem.
det.tip: is only(단지 ~일 뿐이다) / one aspect of the problem(문제의 한 측면)

questions.wa: but this is only one aspect of the problem
accept: but this is only one aspect of the problem

questions.passage: For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location.  Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct.  Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem ①<u>crowding</u> with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: crowding → crowded: '~으로 붐비는' 수동·상태를 나타내는 과거분사 crowded
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem ①<u>crowding</u> with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021.'예요. '갯벌은 다양한 종으로 붐비는 독특한 생태계일 뿐만 아니라 ~'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 밑줄 부분은 앞의 명사 ecosystem(생태계)을 꾸며요. 'be crowded with(~으로 붐비다/가득 차다)'라는 표현처럼, 생태계가 다양한 종으로 '붐비는' 상태를 나타내야 해요.

이런 수동·완료의 의미로 명사를 꾸밀 때는 과거분사를 써요. 그래서 crowding(현재분사)이 아니라 crowded(과거분사)로 고쳐야 맞아요.

정답은 crowded예요.
det.tip: be crowded with ~(~으로 붐비다). 명사를 수동·완료로 꾸미는 과거분사 crowded

'발견될 수 있다'는 조동사 can + 수동태(be + 과거분사)로 써요: can + be + found(발견될 수 있다).

questions.passage: Efforts to Protect Getbol Getbol in Korea was once considered useless muddy land, so much of it has been reclaimed for farming and urbanization.  __________, causing a loss of biodiversity.
questions.stem:

"이것은 갯벌 면적의 감소로 이어졌다." (12단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, area, decline, flats, has, in, led, of, the, this, tidal, to를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것

'갯벌 면적의'는 in the area of tidal flats로 이어요: in + the + area + of + tidal + flats.
